correctness.rationale: For each d>=2, Jacobi complementary minors give S=C/sqrt(sum lambda_i X_i) and H=C sqrt(sum X_i/lambda_i). With Haar U, independent beta ratios Z_k=P_k/P_{k+1} have Beta(k/2,1/2) laws, and both metrics are increasing functions of Z; product association gives association of (S,H), strict for nonballs. For d=3 the normalized Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2) density, determinant Delta and 4H/S^3 Jacobian establish the exact joint density and inverse spectral map, including all constants and support. Direct determinant-geometry, finite sampling, Jacobian and beta reconstruction checks passed; finite tests are not substituted for analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The mathematical novelty assessed is the all-dimensional same-normal positive-association theorem and a complete algebraic joint density and inverse-normal formula for a triaxial ellipsoid. Prior works establish independent marginal section/projection distributions, individual volume integrals, and unrelated inverse shape problems, not the joint two-observable implication. A general Harris association theorem is classical but requires proving the non-obvious common monotone independent-beta representation; all priority claims remain provisional.
residual_risks: An equivalent two-observable Dirichlet pushforward may exist under classical geometric tomography or multivariate stochastic-order terminology.

value.rationale: Central sections and orthogonal shadows are a natural pair of complementary geometric tomography measurements. The theorem completely determines their dependence order for all ellipsoids, the dimension and exact geometry of joint support for every axis multiplicity, and a full bivariate probability density with two-observation inverse-normal reconstruction for triaxial ellipsoids. Marginal distributions and shape invariants do not supply the same information. This is a structural theorem and a natural exact joint classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or numerically sampled table.
